subject: Embeddings model fit validation  1 semantic search metrics & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Embeddings model fit validation  1 summary & next steps

Thanks for the call today  1 good discussion and appreciate the context on your search failures for long-tail queries. Quick recap and proposed next steps for model fit / evals:

Summary of needs
- Improve semantic recall for FAQ+long-tail product queries (few-shot examples in call)
- Maintain sub-200ms per-request latency for embeddings at the scale you estimated (~50 req/s steady, 300 req/s peaks)
- Keep embedding storage costs reasonable (VectorSearch currently ~5M vectors)

Recommended models to benchmark (initial):
- rw-embed-2-xl (1536-d)  1 Redwood-verified, strong semantic recall on product+FAQ workloads
- sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d)  1 cost/latency baseline, good for approximate search
- open-source medium model (e.g., SBERT-based 768-d)  1 evaluate if 1536-d is overkill for your use-case

Key metrics we'll run in the evals
- Recall@10, MRR, and MAP on your labeled relevance set
- Cosine-sim threshold analysis and false-positive rate at selected cutoffs
- Embedding centroid drift (month-over-month) and KS-test for distributional drift
- Storage & throughput: average latency per vector (single-thread), batch throughput (per-GPU / per-CPU), and per-vector storage size

Immediate next steps
1) You: share a 500  1,000 labeled query->relevant-doc pairs (we already have the sample CSV you attached). Please scrub PII.
2) Us: run A/B embedding comparison (rw-embed-2-xl vs MiniLM) and return a short benchmark with recall@10/MRR and throughput table (ETA 48 hours after we receive data).
3) Joint: review results and decide which dimensionality / quantization profile to pilot (int8 vs fp16, tradeoffs documented).

Attachments: vecsearch_eval_promptset_v1.csv (sample labels), we'll add results as PDF and throughput spreadsheet.

Links: full benchmark scaffold -> https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeF_drive_eval

If that plan sounds good I'll kick off the eval as soon as we have the labeled set. Prefer to sync for 30 minutes next Tue/Thu to review results.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation  1 summary & next steps

Great questions  1 answers below and I'll include a short throughput table in the PDF (attached).

1) Ballparks (these are conservative averages from our bench - exact numbers depend on batch size and hardware):
- rw-embed-2-xl (1536-d):
  - single CPU (8 vCPU): ~8  14 ms per vector (batching helps; 64-batch ~3  ms/vector effective)
  - single T4 GPU (fp16): ~0.9  1.5 ms per vector (throughput ~2  4k vectors/s depending on batch)
- MiniLM (384-d):
  - single CPU: ~2  4 ms per vector
  - single GPU: ~0.2  0.6 ms per vector

Storage and network: rw-embed-2-xl at 1536 dims (float32) ~6 KB per vector; int8 quantization reduces raw size ~4x (plus index overhead).

2) Quantization impact (rule-of-thumb from our tests):
- int8 quant: typical recall degradation ~1  4% absolute on recall@10 for product/FAQ workloads; MRR eats slightly more on very fine-grained relevance tests.
- fp16 gives most of the latency/space benefit with minimal quality loss vs fp32. int8 best when storage is primary constraint. We will include quantized vs fp16 vs fp32 curves in the benchmark PDF.

3) Private eval: yes  1 we can run the evaluation in your VPC via Redwood Private (one-off eval job). Neha (copied) is the lead for private deployment and can scope access/NDAs. If you'd rather redact PII we can run on hosted but we understand your preference.

Attachments: benchmark_results_summary.pdf (summary), embeddings_throughput_table.xlsx (per-model throughput numbers). Link to the full scaffold: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcDeF_drive_eval

I'll kick this off as soon as we get the labeled CSV (500  1,000 rows) and confirmation on whether you want a VPC eval.

Best,
Marcus
